issue.title: bench_tui_jk clan fold-level and link-rail j/k benches record TUI stalls (tui_stalls.jsonl non-empty)
issue.description:
Both nodes fail at the stall-record check
`assert not stall_path.exists() or not stall_path.read_text().strip()`, which means `tui_stalls.jsonl`
beside the perf JSONL is non-empty after the bench. Sites: tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk_agents.py:110
(`test_bench_clan_jk_at_each_panel_fold_level`) and tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk_link_rail.py:121
(`test_bench_agents_jk_with_and_without_the_link_rail`). Reproduced in two consecutive runs at master
404b0e2ac2 on athena (load average 18.0, then 4.9). In the link-rail bench, the rail p95-delta
assertions just before the stall check passed, so the stall record alone fails it, not the rail
delta. The sase-1eq.5.1.6 (tui-goldens) phase reproduced both ("clan stall", "link-rail") on a clean
base (phase note #2). The benches do not print the stall rows. A worker should first dump
`tui_stalls.jsonl` from the pytest tmp dir to find the blocking handler, then fix the stall or the
fixture that provokes it. Proposed by phase sase-1eq.5.1.6 note #2 and triaged by the sase-1eq.5.1
land agent. The sase-1eq.5.1 epic adds no navigation work.

evidence.note: Reproduced by phase sase-1q5.5 (epic sase-1q5) on athena 2026-10-30: pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py failed 8 / passed 11 on the clean-tree baseline (592.78s) and again 8 / 11 after the phase (614.51s), with the same failing categories both times (archive warm-open budget; clan fold p95; selected tribe fold level 1; Fleet hung_host, reconnect_churn, event_burst; link-rail stall row; Axe-tab assertion). Not caused by the phase; see sase-1q5.5 note #1. This node set: clan fold-level and link-rail stall rows.

Proposed by sase-1t3.13.1.1 (note #1) and independently reproduced by the sase-1t3.13.1 land agent on 2026-11-18 on athena (load 8-12 on 64 CPUs). Command: pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk_agents.py. test_bench_clan_jk_at_each_panel_fold_level failed in all 6 runs: 2 each at 5b08952c6d, at af07b78ac2, and at HEAD 789e5d0fc5. All three fold levels stayed under the 16 ms p95 budget (worst level p95 about 14 ms). The only failure is the stall-log gate at bench_tui_jk_agents.py:135. It says 'TUI stall log contains actual stalls' and the single row is {'event': 'prompt_activity', 'transition': 'initial', 'state': 'prompt_idle'}. That is a prompt-activity bookkeeping row, not a loop or pump stall. The likely fix is to exclude prompt_activity rows in the bench's actual-stall filter, or to stop the watchdog from writing them to tui_stalls.jsonl. No stalled handler needs hunting for this node.

Reproduced at master 065eda332b on athena (load ~9): test_bench_agents_jk_with_and_without_the_link_rail failed at tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk_agents.py:135 with actual_stalls=[{'event': 'prompt_activity', 'transition': 'initial', 'state': 'prompt_idle', ...}]. That row is activity capture, not a freeze: the filter at bench_tui_jk_agents.py:~120-135 excludes hitch/suppressed counters but not event=='prompt_activity', whereas the shared helper _assert_no_stall_rows in tests/ace/tui/_bench_tui_jk_helpers.py:268 explicitly drops prompt_activity rows. Likely root cause for at least this node: reuse _assert_no_stall_rows (or add the same event filter). Intermittent: a second HEAD run and a pre-50c90e3f2f run failed this node on the 5 ms rail budget instead.

payload.entry: Evidence from tui_acceptance (sase-1tz.2.1.13), HEAD fb85972f27, athena load 8.6/64, 2026-11-20. Not resolved, left open. Neither node records a real stall; the two stall filters disagree. Clan fold p95 next/prev (ms): L1 13.24/11.88, L2 12.38/10.71, L3 12.83/9.76, all under 16. It fails at bench_tui_jk_agents.py:132, whose inline filter drops clean tui_memory_heartbeat rows but not the single prompt_activity initial/prompt_idle row. Link-rail fails at _bench_tui_jk_helpers.py:274 (_assert_no_stall_rows), which drops prompt_activity rows but not a tui_memory_heartbeat row whose loop/pump hitch and suppressed counters are all 0 (first heartbeat at uptime 16 s; the bench runs 44 s). Fix: one shared filter that drops prompt_activity rows and zero-counter heartbeats, used by both nodes.
